# Surah 110: map of image chains

## Chains

### 1. Aid that arrives, and the opening it brings
In 110:1 the verb جَآءَ has two subjects, نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ and ٱلْفَتْحُ, and the dictionaries define each of these nouns by the other. Under فتح they write الفتح = النصر and استفتح = استنصر. The tahdhib phrase quoted under فتح is the Quran's «إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح» (8:19) rewritten with نصر, so the dictionary itself puts جاء and نصر in one sentence and makes فتح their equivalent. The image runs in this order: help is asked for, it comes, the asker gets the upper hand, and what was shut is opened. 110:2 is what can be seen once it has come. 110:3 is the answer to it. A rare sense of نصر, "to come to a land", folds the arrival into the very noun that is said to arrive.
- 110:1 جَآءَ, ج ي ء root_000281 B001: «المجيء كالإتيان لكن المجيء أعم ويقال في الأعيان والمعاني ولمن قصد مكانا أو عملا أو زمانا» (mufradat). Coming is said of things and of abstract matters alike, so aid and opening can be what comes.
- 110:1 نَصْرُ, ن ص ر B001: «نصره الله على عدوه ينصره نصرا» (sihah); «آتاهم الظفر على عدوهم» (maqayis). God's aid that gives the upper hand over an enemy.
- 110:1 نَصْرُ, ن ص ر B003 [fixed expression]: «نصرت بلد كذا إذا أتيته» (maqayis); «نصرت أرض بني فلان أي أتيتها» (tahdhib). نصر as coming to a land.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B004: «الفتح النصر والإظفار واستفتحت استنصرت» (maqayis); «الاستفتاح الاستنصار والفتح النصر» (sihah); «إن تستنصروا فقد جاءكم النصر» (tahdhib); «يحتمل النصرة والظفر والاستفتاح طلب الفتح أو الفتاح وطلب الظفر» (mufradat). The opening is the victory. The asking (استفتاح) comes before the coming.
- Quran:
  - 8:19: God addresses the Meccans, who had asked for a decision before Badr: «إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح». This is the verse the tahdhib phrase glosses.
  - 61:13: God's promise to the believers: «نصر من الله وفتح قريب». The same two nouns in the same order.
  - 48:1–3: God to the Prophet: «إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا ليغفر لك الله ... ويتم نعمته عليك ... وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا». Opening, forgiveness and aid in one sentence.
  - 12:110: the narrator, closing Yusuf: «حتى إذا استيأس الرسل ... جاءهم نصرنا».
  - 2:214: believers and their messenger under trial ask «متى نصر الله» and are answered «ألا إن نصر الله قريب».
  - 6:34: God consoles the Prophet with the earlier messengers, who were patient «حتى أتاهم نصرنا».
  - 3:123: God reminds the believers of Badr: «ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة».
  - 3:126: «وما النصر إلا من عند الله».
  - 5:52: «فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح». The opening is something God brings.

### 2. A land conquered and its people brought under obedience
This chain is the military scene that lies behind the first two ayat. Two armies come into sight of each other and banners are raised. One side wins, the enemy's land is taken (افتتاح دار الحرب), and its people are subjugated (دنت القوم). A city is the place where obedience to those in command is set up. The surah follows this scene up to the people's submission and then changes its direction. What the people enter is دِينِ ٱللَّهِ, the obedience owed to the Worshipped One, not the obedience owed to the conqueror. The one who sees the victory is then told to glorify and to ask forgiveness. In 110:2 the face-off of two armies (تراءى الجمعان) becomes a single seeing: «رَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ».
- 110:1 نَصْرُ, ن ص ر B001: «آتاهم الظفر على عدوهم» (maqayis). Victory over the enemy.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B004: «الفتح افتتاح دار الحرب والفتح النصرة» (ayn). Taking the enemy's territory.
- 110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ, ر ء ي B004: «قوم رئاء وبيوتهم رئاء وتراءى الجمعان» (sihah); «تراءا الجمعان أي تقاربا وتقابلا» (mufradat). Two armies drawing close and facing each other.
- 110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ, ر ء ي B011: «الراية العلامة المنصوبة للرؤية» (mufradat). The banner, raised so that it can be seen.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B004: «دانه دينا أي أذله واستعبده ودينته ملكته» (sihah); «دنت القوم أدينهم إذا أذللتهم» (tahdhib). Subjugating a people.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B001: «أصل واحد إليه يرجع فروعه كلها وهو جنس من الانقياد والذل» (maqayis); «فالدين الطاعة» (maqayis;sihah). The submission that the people enter.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B006: «المدينة كأنها مفعلة سميت بذلك لأنها تقام فيها طاعة ذوي الأمر» (maqayis). The city as the seat of obedience.
- 110:2 أَفْوَاجًا, ف و ج B001: «الفوج القطيع من الناس» (ayn); «الفوج الجماعة المارة المسرعة» (mufradat). Bands of people moving fast, like troops on the march.
- 110:2 ٱللَّهِ, ء ل ه B001: «إله اسما لكل معبود» (mufradat). The obedience belongs to the Worshipped One.
- Quran:
  - 26:61: in the Exodus, Musa's people and Pharaoh's army: «فلما تراءى الجمعان». This is the face-off the dictionary quotes.
  - 33:9: God reminds the believers of the Trench: «إذ جاءتكم جنود فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا وجنودا لم تروها». Coming, armies and seeing.
  - 9:25–26: God on Hunayn: «لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم ... وأنزل جنودا لم تروها».
  - 48:18: God on the pledge under the tree: «وأثابهم فتحا قريبا».
  - 48:27: God confirms the Prophet's dream: «لتدخلن المسجد الحرام ... فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا».
  - 57:10: God ranks those who spent and fought «من قبل الفتح» above those who did so after.
  - 3:83: «أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون». The same phrase دين الله, with submission willing or unwilling.
  - 8:39: «ويكون الدين كله لله».
  - 24:55: God's promise to establish «دينهم الذي ارتضى لهم» and to replace fear with safety.
  - From memory: most reports identify الفتح here with the conquest of Mecca (8 AH).

### 3. A judgment that opens a locked dispute, and redress for the wronged
Two parties are shut in a quarrel, and the judge opens it. The mufradat describes judging with the same image of unlocking: «أزال الإغلاق عنها». The wronged party gets its due (انتصر = انتقم), and the order that follows is one of reckoning and recompense. Heard this way, 110:1 is God's ruling between the Prophet and his people, and 110:2 is people entering a دين that also means judgment and requital. A further sense of دين fits the moment of entry: the judge accepts a man's own word about what lies between him and God.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B003: «الفتح أن تحكم بين قوم يختصمون إليك والفتاح الحاكم» (ayn); «فتح القضية فتاحا فصل الأمر فيها وأزال الإغلاق عنها» (mufradat); «الفتاح الحكومة والقاضي لأنه يفتح مواضع الحق» (tahdhib). Judgment as unlocking.
- 110:1 نَصْرُ, ن ص ر B002: «انتصر الرجل انتقم من ظالمه» (ayn); «انتصر الرجل إذا امتنع من ظالمه» (tahdhib); «إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون» (mufradat). Redress from the oppressor.
- 110:1 نَصْرُ, ن ص ر B001: «عون المظلوم» (ayn;tahdhib). Aid given to the wronged party.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B002: «يوم الدين أي يوم الحكم والحساب والجزاء» (maqayis); «الدين الجزاء والمكافأة» (sihah). Reckoning and requital.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B007: «دينت الرجل في القضاء وفيما بينه وبين الله أي صدقته» (tahdhib); «دينت الرجل تديينا إذا وكلته إلى دينه» (sihah). The judge takes the entrant at his word and leaves the rest to him and God.
- Quran:
  - 7:89: Shuʿayb, threatened with expulsion by his people: «ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق وأنت خير الفاتحين».
  - 26:118: Nuh, rejected: «فافتح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني».
  - 34:26: the Prophet is told to say «ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم».
  - 32:28–29: deniers ask «متى هذا الفتح». The answer: «يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم». Once the decision comes, a late entry no longer helps.
  - 14:15: the messengers against their peoples: «واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد».
  - 40:78: «فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق». Coming, followed by judgment.
  - 42:39: believers «إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون». The mufradat quotes this verse.
  - 22:39–40: permission to fight for those expelled from their homes: «وإن الله على نصرهم لقدير ... ولينصرن الله من ينصره».
  - 30:47: «فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين». Vengeance and aid in one verse.
  - 17:33: the heir of someone killed wrongfully: «إنه كان منصورا». Redress, framed with «إنه كان» as in 110:3.
  - 22:60: «لينصرنه الله إن الله لعفو غفور». Redress followed by forgiveness.

### 4. A gate opened, and band after band going in
This is the plainest chain in the surah. A shut thing is opened wide (باب فتح), and فتح also names the key. The opening is a فاتحة, "that by which what follows is opened", and what it opens onto is the entering of 110:2. The bands come up, pass through a wide gap between two rises (فائجة), and go in, entering being the opposite of going out. At the threshold, people who enter ask leave and greet, and the dictionary explains that act with إنس and دخل together. Those entering are فوجا بعد فوج, one band after another through the same opening.
- 110:1 جَآءَ, ج ي ء root_000281 B001: «جاء يجيء مجيئا» (maqayis;mufradat). Coming up to the opening.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B001: «خلاف الإغلاق ونقيض الإغلاق» (all six sources); «فتحت الباب وغيره فتحا» (maqayis;sihah); «باب فتح أي واسع مفتوح» (maqayis;ayn;sihah;tahdhib;mufradat). The gate thrown wide.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B006: «المفتاح مفتاح الباب وكل مستغلق» (sihah). The key.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B002: «فاتحة الشيء أوله» (sihah); «فاتحة كل شيء مبدؤه الذي يفتح به ما بعده» (mufradat). An opening that starts what comes after it.
- 110:2 يَدْخُلُونَ, د خ ل B001: «أصل مطرد منقاس وهو الولوج» (maqayis); «دخلت الدار وغيرها وأدخلت غيري» (jamhara); «الدخول نقيض الخروج ويستعمل في المكان والزمان والأعمال» (mufradat). Going in, the opposite of going out.
- 110:2 أَفْوَاجًا, ف و ج B002: «الفائجة متسع ما بين كل مرتفعين من غلظ أو رمل» (sihah); «الفائج البساط الواسع من الأرض» (tahdhib). The wide ground the bands cross.
- 110:2 أَفْوَاجًا, ف و ج B001: «أفواج أي فوجا بعد فوج» (tahdhib). Band after band.
- 110:2 ٱلنَّاسَ, ء ن س B007: «حتى تستأنسوا معناه حتى تستأذنوا وإنما هو حتى تسلموا وتستأنسوا السلام عليكم أأدخل» (tahdhib); «حتى تستأنسوا أي تجدوا إيناسا» (mufradat). Asking leave at the threshold. The dictionary joins the roots of ٱلنَّاسَ and يَدْخُلُونَ in one phrase.
- 110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ, ر ء ي B003: «الرؤيا ما يرى في المنام» (mufradat). The entry the Prophet had seen in a dream (48:27).
- Quran:
  - 39:71 and 39:73: the final driving of people to their abodes, «وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها ... فادخلوها خالدين». The scene continues in 39:74–75 with «الحمد لله» and «وترى الملائكة ... يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق». Coming, opened gates, groups, entering, seeing and tasbih bi-hamd all in one scene.
  - 78:18–19: the Day of the Trumpet: «فتأتون أفواجا وفتحت السماء فكانت أبوابا». Bands, an opening and gates.
  - 27:83: «ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا».
  - 67:8: «كلما ألقي فيها فوج». A band going in the other direction.
  - 38:59: «هذا فوج مقتحم معكم». A band breaking in.
  - 5:23: two God-fearing men to Musa's people at the land: «ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون». Entering the gate is the victory.
  - 2:58 and 7:161: God to Banu Israʾil at the town: «وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم». Entering the gate together with prostration and a plea for forgiveness.
  - 24:27: «لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها». This is the verse the tahdhib phrase glosses.
  - 13:23: «جنات عدن يدخلونها ... والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب».
  - 48:27: «لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق لتدخلن المسجد الحرام ... فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا». A dream, an entry and an opening.

### 5. The master's house and the obedience owed in it
This chain is the domain that people enter. A رب is the owner of a house (رب الدار). دين is obedience, and the dictionary writes «الدين لله», joining دين with the divine name. A city is the place where obedience is kept, and one sense of سبح is a name for the sacred land itself. So the surah's three references to God form one household. The aid is نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ, the obedience entered is دِينِ ٱللَّهِ, and the response goes to رَبِّكَ. The people go into a house whose owner is the one being praised, not into the house of whoever saw them come in.
- 110:1 and 110:2 ٱللَّهِ, ء ل ه B001: «فالإله الله تعالى لأنه معبود» (maqayis); «التأله التعبد» (ayn). The same Worshipped One owns the aid and the obedience.
- 110:2 يَدْخُلُونَ, د خ ل B001: «دخلت البيت وادخل وتدخل الشيء» (sihah). Entering a house.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B001: «الدين لله طاعته والتعبد له» (tahdhib). The dictionary joins دين and لله.
- 110:2 دِينِ, د ي ن B006: «المدينة كأنها مفعلة سميت بذلك لأنها تقام فيها طاعة ذوي الأمر» (maqayis). The inhabited place of obedience.
- 110:3 رَبِّكَ, ر ب ب B001: «رب الدار ورب الفرس» (mufradat); «ورب كل شيء مالكه» (jamhara); «يكون الرب: السيد المطاع» (tahdhib). The owner of the house, the master who is obeyed.
- 110:3 فَسَبِّحْ, س ب ح B008: «سَبّوحة البلد الحرام ويقال واد بعرفات» (sihah). The sacred territory carries the name.
- Quran:
  - 106:3: Quraysh are told «فليعبدوا رب هذا البيت».
  - 3:96–97: «إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذي ببكة ... ومن دخله كان آمنا». House, people, entering, «كان».
  - 48:27: entering the sanctuary as the promised outcome.
  - 109:6: «لكم دينكم ولي دين». The dīn as the thing that belongs to someone.
  - 39:3, from memory: «ألا لله الدين الخالص».

### 6. Seeing the crowd
110:2 is built around one act of sight: «وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ». The dictionary ties the two words together. Humans (إنس) are "named for their being visible" (سموا لظهورهم), and آنس means "to see". The pupil of the eye is called إنسان because a small human figure "is seen" in it, and the mirror is "that in which the forms of things are seen". The crowd that is seen is defined as «الجماعة من الناس», moving fast. The image is a field of vision filling with human bands. 110:3 is what is said in answer to that sight.
- 110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ, ر ء ي B001: «نظر وإبصار بعين أو بصيرة» (maqayis); «رأيت بعيني رؤية ورأيته رأي العين» (ayn;tahdhib). Sight with the eye, or with insight.
- 110:2 ٱلنَّاسَ, ء ن س B001: «الإنس خلاف الجن وسموا لظهورهم» (maqayis;mufradat); «الإنس جماعة الناس» (tahdhib). Humans as the visible kind.
- 110:2 ٱلنَّاسَ, ء ن س B002: «آنست الشيء إذا رأيته وآنسته إذا سمعته» (maqayis); «آنسته أبصرته» (sihah). The root of ٱلنَّاسَ itself means to catch sight of. The dictionary glosses it with رأى.
- 110:2 ٱلنَّاسَ, ء ن س B005: «إنسان العين المثال الذي يرى في السواد أي سواد العين» (sihah). The little human figure in the pupil.
- 110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ, ر ء ي B006: «المرآة ما يرى فيه صورة الأشياء» (mufradat). The surface on which the scene shows.
- 110:2 أَفْوَاجًا, ف و ج B001: «الفوج الجماعة من الناس والجمع أفواج» (maqayis); «الفوج الجماعة المارة المسرعة» (mufradat). The dictionary joins أفواج and الناس. The bands are seen in motion.
- Quran:
  - 7:143: Musa «لما جاء ... لميقاتنا» asks «رب أرني أنظر إليك», is told «لن تراني», and on recovering says «سبحانك تبت إليك». Coming, seeing, tasbih and return in one scene.
  - 39:75: «وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم». The addressee is shown a throng engaged in tasbih bi-hamd.
  - 22:18: «ألم تر أن الله يسجد له ... وكثير من الناس». Seeing people in worship.
  - 30:48: «فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله». Seeing rain come out, which ties into chain 9.

### 7. Being seen: display, boasting and claimed praise, and their reversal
This chain is the reverse of chain 6. The dictionary joins the surah's رأيت and الناس in the phrase for showing off: «فعل ذلك رئاء الناس وهو أن يفعل شيئا ليراه الناس». In 110:2 the addressee sees the people. In رياء a man acts so that the people see him. فتح has a sense of swelling with pride over one's wealth or learning. حمد has a fixed expression for claiming praise by reminding people of a favour, and that phrase too contains الناس. Against all of this, 110:3 orders a praise that belongs to «رَبِّكَ» alone and a tasbih that clears God of every fault. The credit for the opening and for the crowd goes back to its owner, and istighfar covers whatever self-credit clings to the one who saw.
- 110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ, ر ء ي B005: «وراءى فلان يرائي وفعل ذلك رئاء الناس وهو أن يفعل شيئا ليراه الناس» (maqayis); «يرآءون الناس إذا أبصرهم الناس صلوا وإذا لم يروهم تركوا الصلاة» (tahdhib). Acting to be seen. The dictionary joins the surah's رأى and الناس.
- 110:1 وَٱلْفَتْحُ, ف ت ح B009: «الفتحة تفتح الإنسان بما عنده من أموال أو أدب يتطاول به» (ayn); «الفتحة تفتح الإنسان بما عنده من ملك أو أدب يتطاول به» (tahdhib). Jamhara records «الفتحة التيه والتكبر» and adds «وأحسبها مولدة», doubting that the word is old Arabic. Swelling with what one has.
- 110:3 بِحَمْدِ, ح م د B005 [fixed expression]: «فلان يتحمد علي أي يمن» (sihah); «من أنفق ماله على نفسه فلا يتحمد به إلى الناس» (sihah;tahdhib). Claiming praise from the people for a favour.
- 110:3 بِحَمْدِ, ح م د B001: «الحمد نقيض الذم» (maqayis;ayn;jamhara;sihah;tahdhib); «الحمد الثناء» (ayn;tahdhib;mufradat). Praise, here bound to «رَبِّكَ».
- 110:3 فَسَبِّحْ, س ب ح B002: «التسبيح وهو تنزيه الله من كل سوء» (maqayis); «سبحان تنزيه وتبرئة» (jamhara). Clearing God of fault, which leaves no fault, and no credit, with anyone else.
- 110:3 وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ, غ ف ر B002: «المغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب» (mufradat). Protection for the one who sought it.

### 8. The whole people coming, none held back
A fixed expression under غفر describes a people arriving all together, «جاء القوم جماء الغفير», which the sihah explains as «جاءوا بجماعتهم: الشريف والوضيع، ولم يتخلف أحد، وكانت فيهم كثرة». The phrase uses the surah's own verb جاء and the root of its اسْتَغْفِرْ, and it describes the scene of 110:2: the people as a whole, in great numbers, high and low together. One sense of رب is a huge multitude (الربيون: الألوف), and the sihah defines it with الناس. A fixed expression under جاء means beating someone by coming more often than he does. So جاء, غفر and رب each carry a picture of a great host arriving.

### 9. Rain, the channels, the gathering basin and the watering
A connected picture of water runs through the roots of 110:1. نصر is rain that soaks the land and makes it grow, and نصر القوم means the people got rain. Its plural النواصر names watercourses that "come from far off until they fall into the gathering-place of water". In that phrase the dictionary uses the verb تجيء and, for the place, the same «مجتمع الماء» it uses to define جيأة, a sense of the root of جَآءَ. فتح is water coming out of a spring, a river, land watered by flow, and the first rain of the season. The bands of 110:2 cross wide ground between two rises. In one dictionary sense, «يدخلون» is leading camels to the trough for a second drink, or bringing them all in at once in a crush. رب names the layered cloud, "called so because it raises the plants", and «الماء الكثير». The surah's 110:3 has no water word. But in the Quran its own terms, «استغفروا ربكم ... إنه كان», are the formula that brings down rain (71:10–12; 11:52). So the chain closes on the third ayah.

### 10. A rite: opening, praise, glorification, prostration, forgiveness
The dictionary joins فتح and حمد in one phrase: «كل ما بدأت به فقد استفتحته وبه سميت الحمد فاتحة الكتاب». Under فتح it also gives «افتتاح الصلاة التكبيرة الأولى», and under سبح it gives «السبحة وهي الصلاة» and «السبحات مواضع السجود». Read with these senses, the surah moves through the parts of a prayer. It opens (الفتح, the فاتحة, which is الحمد), then comes tasbih, which is the prayer itself and the places of prostration, then praise, then istighfar. ### 11. Cover: the helmet and the protective covering
The concrete root of غفر is covering that protects. Its examples are the helmet of mail over the head, a cloth that guards a veil from oil, and a patch that covers a bowstring notch. The mufradat defines it as «إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس», putting on something that guards from soiling, and defines God's forgiveness the same way: guarding the servant from being touched by punishment. 110:1 sets an armed scene and 110:2 shows a gate opened and a crowd going in. Into that scene «وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ» brings asking for a cover over oneself. From memory: on the day of the conquest the Prophet entered Mecca with the مغفر, the helmet, on his head (Bukhari, Muslim, from Anas).

### 12. Coming, going in, staying, turning back
These are the verbs of motion the surah strings together. The mufradat describes coming (جاء) and entering (دخل) with almost the same words: جاء is said «لمن قصد مكانا أو عملا أو زمانا», and دخل «يستعمل في المكان والزمان والأعمال». Both are movements into place, time and deeds. The sihah defines one sense of سبح as «التصرف في المعاش والمنقلب والجيئة والذهاب», using the noun of جاء itself. توب is «الرجوع», returning. The dictionary also says God "returns to" the servant, and it says so with forgiveness: «تاب الله عليه أي عاد عليه بالمغفرة». So the surah's motion goes like this. Aid comes toward the Prophet, people go in, the Prophet keeps going and coming in tasbih, and God is the one who turns back to whoever turns back, again and again (توّاب). One sense of رب is staying put in a place, which contrasts with all this movement. Another sense of توب is offering someone the chance to return, so the return is offered as well as accepted.

### 13. The passage that can be seen, and the inside that cannot
دخل has an outer face and an inner one. Going in can be seen. The داخلة of a man is "the inner side of his affair", and دخل is also a hidden flaw or concealed enmity, and a palm rotten in its core. The people are "named for their being visible". What 110:2 shows is a passage that can be seen, and the eye certifies that much. The judge's تديين leaves a man's inner state to him and to God. 110:3 answers what the eye cannot certify with tasbih and with a request for cover.

### 14. Opened treasuries and goods given
نصر is, by one root definition, «إتيان خير وإيتائه», the coming of good and the giving of it, and its noun is «العطاء». جاء with بـ is bringing something and presenting it. The مفتح is a treasury and its مفاتح are its treasures. فتح is also relief from worry and poverty lifted by a gift of wealth. حمد includes thanks, and a fixed expression under it is acknowledging someone's favours (أياديه ونعمه). رب includes completing a favour (رب الرجل النعمة ... إذا تممها) and the favour itself. Heard together, 110:1 is a treasury opened and a gift brought, and 110:3's praise is thanks for it.

### 15. Newcomers taken in and raised to completion
The people who enter in 110:2 are newcomers to a body that already exists. A دخيل is "one who is among a tribe though not of them", someone you bring into your affairs. أنس is being at ease with no estrangement. The رب of 110:3 is the one who brings a thing up "state by state to the limit of completeness". The same root names the step-parent and the foster-child (الراب, الربيب): someone who takes charge of raising a child not born to them. The dictionary also gives رب for repairing a waterskin with rubb and for preparing medicine with honey. So entry opens a household: outsiders are taken in, the estrangement ends, and they are raised and mended toward completion.

### 16. The task finished, the term come
جاء is said of a time that arrives. سبح is defined as «الفراغ», a span with nothing more to do. حمد has a form for one's utmost (حماداك = قصاراك, «غايتك وفعلك المحمود»). رب is completing a thing to its limit. One noun from the root of كان names an old man who looks back and says "I was" (كنتي). توب is returning. Heard in this sequence, the surah tells of a work brought to its end. The aid has come, the gate is open and the people are in. What is left is to glorify, to ask forgiveness, and to turn back to the Lord. From memory: Ibn ʿAbbas, asked by ʿUmar, read the surah as God telling the Prophet that his term (أجل) was near, and ʿUmar agreed (Bukhari).

### 17. A wound gathers, is opened, and may relapse
The dictionary uses the surah's verb جاء and the root of its اسْتَغْفِرْ for the course of a wound. «جاءت جائية الجراح» is pus gathering in the wound, and «غفر الجرح ... نكس» is the wound breaking open again after healing. فتح is opening a closed thing. رب is preparing a remedy and mending. In this sequence, what had gathered comes to a head (110:1), is opened, and the opened state becomes good. Istighfar (110:3) then answers the danger that the wound breaks open again after the recovery.

## Ayat

**110:1 إِذَا جَآءَ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْفَتْحُ**
- 1 Aid arrives: جَآءَ gives the arrival, نَصْرُ the aid over the enemy (and coming to a land), and ٱلْفَتْحُ the opening that is the victory. Whole scene: help long asked for comes from God, and what was shut is opened. People are seen pouring in, and the one who received it praises his Lord.
- 2 Conquest: نَصْرُ is the upper hand and ٱلْفَتْحُ the taking of territory. Whole scene: two armies face each other, one prevails and the land is taken. Its people are seen entering, in bands, into the obedience owed to God rather than to the victor, and the victor is told to glorify and ask forgiveness.
- 3 Judgment: ٱلْفَتْحُ is the verdict that unlocks a dispute, and نَصْرُ the redress of the wronged. Whole scene: God rules between the Prophet and his people. The wronged party has its due, people enter an order of reckoning where their word is taken, and the one vindicated still asks forgiveness.
- 4 Gate opened: جَآءَ is coming up to the gate, ٱلْفَتْحُ the gate thrown wide (with key and فاتحة). Whole scene: a gate opens wide, bands come up across open ground, greet, and go in one after another. Then praise and forgiveness are spoken at the end of the entry.
- 5 Master's house: ٱللَّهِ is the owner of the aid. Whole scene: aid from God, people entering God's obedience, and praise to the Lord who owns the house.
- 7 Being seen: ٱلْفَتْحُ carries the sense of swelling with what one has (jamhara doubts the word). Whole scene: a great success is seen by all. Its credit is cleared from the one who saw it, sent back to his Lord in praise, and covered by forgiveness.
- 8 Whole people: جَآءَ is the verb of «جاء القوم جماء الغفير», and it also means outdoing by many comings. Whole scene: the whole people come, high and low, none held back. The verb and the root of the cover (غفر) together describe that arrival.
- 9 Rain: نَصْرُ is rain and tributaries, جَآءَ the basin, ٱلْفَتْحُ water released and the first rains. Whole scene: rain falls, channels carry it from far off into the basin and it is let out. Herds crowd to the water in bands, and the Lord of the cloud is answered with the words that bring rain.
- 10 Rite: ٱلْفَتْحُ is the opening of the prayer (التكبيرة الأولى) and the فاتحة, which is الحمد. Whole scene: the rite opens, people enter a worship, and it moves to tasbih, praise, prostration and forgiveness.
- 11 Cover: ٱلْفَتْحُ is the laying bare that a cover answers. Whole scene: an armed opening and a crowd entering, then a request for the helmet-like cover of forgiveness.
- 12 Return: جَآءَ is coming toward a place, a deed or a time. Whole scene: aid comes, people go in, the addressee keeps on in tasbih, and God returns to whoever returns, again and again.
- 14 Treasuries: جَآءَ is bringing in, نَصْرُ the gift, ٱلْفَتْحُ the treasury, the key and relief. Whole scene: a treasury opened and a gift brought, and praise as thanks to the Lord who completes the favour.
- 15 Newcomers: ٱلْفَتْحُ is the beginning that opens what follows. Whole scene: an opening begins a household. Outsiders are taken in, estrangement ends, and the Lord raises them stage by stage.
- 16 Task finished: جَآءَ is the coming of a time. Whole scene: the work is brought to its end, the time is free, and the one who did it glorifies, asks forgiveness and turns back to the Lord.
- 17 Wound: جَآءَ is pus gathering, ٱلْفَتْحُ the opening. Whole scene: what had gathered is opened and released, and forgiveness is asked against a relapse after the recovery.

**110:2 وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا**
- 2 Conquest: وَرَأَيْتَ carries the armies facing each other and the banner, دِينِ subjugation, obedience and the city, and أَفْوَاجًا troops on the move. The whole conquest scene is as given under 110:1.
- 3 Judgment: دِينِ is reckoning and requital, and also the judge accepting a man's word (تديين). The whole judgment scene is as given under 110:1.
- 4 Gate opened: يَدْخُلُونَ is going in, أَفْوَاجًا band after band through a wide gap, and ٱلنَّاسَ the greeting and leave-seeking at the threshold (استئناس). وَرَأَيْتَ points to the dream of entry. The whole gate scene is as given under 110:1.
- 5 Master's house: يَدْخُلُونَ is entering a house, دِينِ the obedience that belongs to God (الدين لله), and ٱللَّهِ its owner. The whole house scene is as given under 110:1.
- 6 Seeing: وَرَأَيْتَ is sight with eye or insight. ٱلنَّاسَ is the visible kind, whose root means "to see", and the human figure in the pupil. أَفْوَاجًا is fast-moving bands. Whole scene: a field of vision fills with human bands entering God's obedience, and the one who sees answers with tasbih and praise of his Lord.
- 7 Being seen: وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ is the reverse of «رئاء الناس ... ليراه الناس». The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 8 Whole people: ٱلنَّاسَ is the body of people and أَفْوَاجًا plural upon plural. The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 9 Rain: أَفْوَاجًا is the open ground between rises, and يَدْخُلُونَ herds brought to the trough in a crush and brought back for more. The whole rain scene is as given under 110:1.
- 10 Rite: دِينِ and ٱللَّهِ are worship (التعبد). The whole rite scene is as given under 110:1.
- 11 Cover: يَدْخُلُونَ is the inner edge of a wrap, the side of the garment next to the body. The whole cover scene is as given under 110:1.
- 12 Return: يَدْخُلُونَ is going in, the opposite of going out, into a place, a time or deeds. The whole motion scene is as given under 110:1.
- 13 Inside: وَرَأَيْتَ is sight, whose reach is the visible. ٱلنَّاسَ is the visible kind. يَدْخُلُونَ is the crossing, the inner side of a man's affair, and the hidden flaw. دِينِ is leaving the inside to the man and God. Whole scene: the eye sees a real crossing into God's obedience but not each heart. What it cannot certify is met with tasbih and with a request for cover.
- 15 Newcomers: يَدْخُلُونَ is the outsider taken in, ٱلنَّاسَ estrangement turning to ease, and دِينِ habit to be formed. The whole scene is as given under 110:1.

**110:3 فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ تَوَّابًۢا**
- 5 Master's house: رَبِّكَ is the owner of the house and the master who is obeyed. فَسَبِّحْ is a name of the sacred land. The whole house scene is as given under 110:1.
- 6 Seeing: the whole answer to what was seen. Tasbih bi-hamd is what the throng in 39:75 is shown doing.
- 7 Being seen: فَسَبِّحْ clears God of all fault, بِحَمْدِ gives praise that belongs to the Lord and carries the fixed expression for claiming praise from people, and وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ is cover. The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 8 Whole people: وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ shares its root with «جماء الغفير», and رَبِّكَ carries the multitude (الربيون). The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 9 Rain: فَسَبِّحْ is swimming and swift motion through water, and رَبِّكَ the rain-cloud and abundant gathered water. «اسْتَغْفِرْهُ ... إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ» is the Quran's rain-bringing formula (71:10–12, 11:52). The whole rain scene is as given under 110:1.
- 10 Rite: فَسَبِّحْ is prayer and the places of prostration, بِحَمْدِ the content of the فاتحة, and وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ asking forgiveness. The whole rite scene is as given under 110:1.
- 11 Cover: وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ is cover, helmet and protective covering. The whole cover scene is as given under 110:1.
- 12 Return: فَسَبِّحْ is coming and going about one's work, and رَبِّكَ abiding. تَوَّابًۢا is returning, God returning with forgiveness many times, and return offered. The whole motion scene is as given under 110:1.
- 13 Inside: وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ is the cover laid over what the eye cannot see. The whole scene is as given under 110:2.
- 14 Treasuries: بِحَمْدِ is thanks and acknowledging favours, and رَبِّكَ completing a favour and the favour itself. The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 15 Newcomers: رَبِّكَ is raising by stages, the foster-parent, and mending and remedy. تَوَّابًۢا is the invitation to return held open. The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 16 Task finished: فَسَبِّحْ is the time freed, بِحَمْدِ one's praiseworthy utmost, رَبِّكَ completion, كَانَ time gone by and the old man's "I was", and تَوَّابًۢا the return. The whole scene is as given under 110:1.
- 17 Wound: وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ is relapse after healing (the fixed expression), and رَبِّكَ treatment and setting right. The whole wound scene is as given under 110:1.
- 1 Aid arrives, 3 Judgment: 110:3 has no member word in these two chains. Their scenes end in its commands, as given under 110:1.

## Not carried

- victory becomes report: its member "transmitting news or poetry" belongs to ر و ي, an echo root the gateway withholds, not the root of رأيت. Without it, nothing joins the event to retelling.
- opening as cutover: its cutting member (تب إذا قطع) belongs to ت ب ب, an echo root the gateway withholds, not the root of توّاب.
- counted waves: tahdhib calls the prayer-bead سبحة «كلمة مولدة», and no wording in the surah joins counting to the bands.
- Members dropped inside chains that were carried, for the same echo-root reason: ر ء ي "carrying water" and "quenching" (released water cascade, hydraulic return cycle) are ر و ي. "Nourishment and growth" (opening as postvictory beginning, entry begins cultivation, social irrigation) is ر ب و B005, not ر ب ب B005, which is the foster-parent sense. "Readiness, straightness, continuation" for توّاب (entry as recurrent return, processual repair, opening is threshold, hydraulic return cycle, post victory relapse, counted waves) is ت ب ب استتب. "Transactional surplus" for رب (collective accounting) is ر ب و ربا. د ي ن B003 (debt) in collective accounting: no wording in the surah carries a ledger image.
